text: Ironically, sexclusivity, which we treat as the basis of romance, started out as that kind of bureaucratic record-keeping. By the 17th century, when England began mass urbanization by forcing peasants off their land, it became the legal definition of marriage. As for what comes naturally to us underneath that law, I’m not trying to say we’re just like bonobos, but the academic consensus is that humans tend toward flexible pair-bonding, with a propensity for occasional infidelity.
reader: someone reading an essay on romance for advice they can use in their own dating and relationships
